source.title: How Long Does Infinite Width Last? Signal Propagation in Long-Range Linear Recurrences

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figure labels are flattened, but the stated results and figure descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies signal energies at random initialization in recurrent models. It does not measure gradient-based training error, convergence, or trainability in the classification settings covered by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's signal-energy and signal-growth results concern initialization behavior, not training classification error. They do not test a listed version; the relevant findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study derives and numerically checks signal propagation at random initialization in recurrent models. It does not measure training error, learning speed, trainable depth, optimization minima, learning-rate recovery, or batch-normalization benefits. Its signal and backward-gradient energy results are related to V4 but do not test V4's claimed training outcomes; Section 5.1 explicitly leaves training analysis to future work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors identify √n as the critical recurrent depth scale for departures from infinite-width signal-energy predictions under Gaussian initialization. Their experiments suggest amplification also occurs in ReLU and LeakyReLU recurrences, while untied feedforward counterparts remain stable in the tested regime. They leave consequences for training to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives and studies signal propagation at random initialization; it does not run gradient-based classification training or compare training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Signal behavior varies with recurrent depth relative to width, weight sharing versus independent step-wise weights, real versus complex Gaussian weights, and activation in the nonlinear experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: For linear recurrences with complex Gaussian weights, infinite-width signal-energy predictions hold below recurrent depth √n, acquire nontrivial corrections at depth proportional to √n, and exhibit exploding amplification when √n ≪ depth ≪ n. Monte Carlo experiments validate the critical profiles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent weight sharing makes finite-width corrections to expected signal energy substantial at depths proportional to the square root of width.

fits_no_version.finding: Real Gaussian recurrent models have signal energies at least as large as their complex counterparts under the stated assumptions; experiments show larger energies and qualitatively similar amplification. The real-LRU bound requires nonnegative traces of cross-time input correlations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-width recurrent signal amplification persists with real Gaussian initialization, with an analytical lower bound subject to the model's input assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: ReLU and LeakyReLU recurrences with variance-preserving Gaussian initialization show rapid signal growth, while corresponding feedforward models with independent weights at each step remain near energy one.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-matched variance preservation does not ensure stable expected signal energy in long recurrences with shared weights.

fits_no_version.finding: Remark 2 analytically shows that backward-gradient energy in the linear RNN is proportional to Qn,t and therefore follows the same depth-width scaling laws. This is an initialization result rather than a training-dynamics result.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forward signal energy and backward-gradient energy share the same depth-width scaling in the specified randomly initialized linear recurrence.

record.problems: The exact theory is for linear recurrences with complex Gaussian weights; the real-weight result is a lower bound and its numerical results are shown in figures without exact values. Nonlinear results are numerical and the paper says their theoretical characterization remains open. No training classification outcomes are measured.

Learning speed and trainable depth under activation-matched initialization; orthogonal-versus-Gaussian tanh training; and training 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks. Initialization signal-energy stability alone does not test these outcomes.

All parts: accuracy gain, training speed, learning-rate tolerance, batch-normalization comparisons, and Fixup training.

Training error as depth changes, identity shortcuts, special initialization, and normalization-free residual training.

rows.operation_detail: Measures normalized expected squared hidden-state norm Qn,k under complex Gaussian weights of variance 1/n.

rows.subject: Linear recurrent network (RNN)
rows.operation_detail: Measures normalized expected squared hidden-state norm Qn,k under complex Gaussian weights of variance 1/n.
rows.value: Qn,k ∼ [n/((k + 1)(k + 2))] exp(nΨ(k/n)), where Ψ(x) = (1 + x) log(1 + x) − x
rows.note: The authors say both signal energies diverge in the stated joint limit.
rows.check: The supercritical asymptotic matches the text. Exploding signal energy at initialization is not an observed training failure.

rows.value: Sn,t ∼ (n²/t³) exp(nΨ(t/n)), where Ψ(x) = (1 + x) log(1 + x) − x
rows.note: The authors say both signal energies diverge in the stated joint limit.
rows.check: The supercritical LRU asymptotic matches the text. It does not measure optimization or trainable depth.
